title: vibe-animator: launch trailer
notes: Line fields: id, voice (NARRATOR|DIRECTOR|KHWARIZMI|STUDENT), mood (wonder|struggle|insight|hope; insight = 2-4 s accent on the cue word, not a bed), cue_word (the word the line's key animation lands on), text, refs, visual, optional hold (s of silence after the line) and short markers. HARD RULE: no nutrition/health content, no channel names, no mention of the project the pipeline was built on. Each chapter ends with the film-strip pull-back to the next segment. DIRECTOR lines carry typed: true (the prompt is typed on screen in step with the voice; scenes use q.typed(id, t)).

lines.text: Make me a trailer.
lines.visual: Engraved-plate house style, warm paper. A cursor blinks; the prompt types itself, letter by letter, finishing on 'trailer'.

short.hook_title: One prompt made this whole video

lines.text: One sentence. That is the whole brief.
lines.visual: The typed line sits alone on the paper; an amber underline draws under it on 'sentence'.

lines.text: Script, voices, scenes and cuts: Claude Code agents make them all.
lines.visual: Four engraved labels (SCRIPT, VOICES, SCENES, CUTS) branch from the prompt; on 'agents' small agent nodes light up under each.

lines.text: A language model. A ninth-century master. A million-dollar problem. A page from 1619.
lines.visual: Four half-second flash frames from this trailer's own segments, one per phrase: embedding cloud, watercolor Baghdad, exploding curve, the Kepler page. No footage from anywhere else.

lines.text: Watch it build.
lines.visual: On 'build' the prompt's letters break into particles that rush into the first frame; the camera pulls back to reveal the vertical 35 mm film strip, which slides on.

short.hook_title: One prompt made this whole video

lines.text: Explain attention. Twenty seconds.
lines.visual: Dark math look, glowing vector strokes. The prompt types in a corner; the sentence 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired' writes in as tokens.

short.hook_title: How an LLM picks its next word

lines.text: A language model turns each word into a point in space, where related meanings sit close together.
lines.visual: On 'space' the tokens lift into a slowly rotating 3D embedding cloud; 'cat' and 'mat' drift near each other. All code original.

lines.text: Each word looks back and weighs the words before. Here, "it" reaches for "the cat".
lines.visual: Faint attention lines from the last token to every earlier token; on the quoted 'it' the line from 'it' to 'the cat' brightens. Small corner tag: ILLUSTRATIVE.

lines.text: Then it gives every word it knows a probability, and bets on one.
lines.visual: Probability bars race for the next-word slot; on 'bets' one bar is sampled and drops into the sentence as the next token. Pull-back to the film strip.

short.hook_title: How an LLM picks its next word

lines.text: Baghdad, ninth century. Complete the square.
lines.visual: Watercolor wash: a Baghdad courtyard, a master and a student at a table. The prompt types over the wash in ink.

short.hook_title: The 1,200-year-old trick behind the quadratic formula

lines.text: A square and ten roots make thirty-nine. I am stuck.
lines.visual: Clean ink over the wash: an x-by-x square, then on 'ten' a 10-wide-by-x rectangle beside it; the label '= 39' (no symbols spoken). Student character is dramatized.

lines.text: Split the ten in half. Five on two sides.
lines.visual: On 'half' the rectangle splits; two 5-wide strips swing onto two sides of the square.

lines.text: Now a corner is missing: five by five.
lines.visual: On 'corner' the empty 5x5 gap glows amber; '25' writes inside it.

lines.text: Fill it, and the square is whole: eight by eight. The root is three.
lines.visual: On 'fill' the corner fills and the perfect 8x8 square locks (insight sting); 39 + 25 = 64 writes beside it; the side reads 5 + 3, and the 3 glows.

lines.text: That was al-Khwarizmi, and his al-jabr gave algebra its name.
lines.visual: The master's name inks in beneath the figure; on 'al-jabr' the word unfolds into 'algebra'.

lines.text: He wrote it all in words. Centuries later, the picture became a formula.
lines.visual: A 'centuries later' caption first; only then does the figure morph into symbols, and on 'formula' the quadratic formula assembles. Pull-back to the film strip.

short.hook_title: The 1,200-year-old trick behind the quadratic formula

lines.text: P versus NP. Make it hurt.
lines.visual: Dark math look. The prompt types; the background dims a step on 'hurt'.

short.hook_title: Checking is easy. Is finding easy?

lines.text: Checking a finished puzzle takes a second. Finding the answer may not.
lines.visual: A filled sudoku grid ticks green row by row within one second; beside it a search tree starts branching. No 'NP-complete' caption.

lines.text: As the puzzle grows, the search explodes.
lines.visual: The grid grows larger; a plot race of n squared, n cubed and 2 to the n; on 'explodes' the 2^n curve goes vertical and the tree fills the frame.

lines.text: P equals NP would mean anything checkable in polynomial time is also solvable in polynomial time.
lines.visual: On-screen definition in LaTeX, 'polynomial time' on both sides; on 'solvable' the two halves of the definition link with an equals sign and a question mark.

lines.text: Nobody knows. A proof is worth a million dollars.
lines.visual: On 'million' a card: '$1,000,000 Millennium Prize'.

lines.text: AI might help find that proof. On other problems, it has already found new mathematics.
lines.visual: Two small cards on 'mathematics': 'FunSearch: new cap-set constructions (2023)' and 'AlphaEvolve: improved algorithms (2025)', each stamped 'not P vs NP'. Pull-back to the film strip.

short.hook_title: Checking is easy. Is finding easy?

lines.text: Kepler. Show me the actual page.
refs: Harmonices Mundi (Linz, 1619), Book V ch. III, p. 189
lines.visual: Engraved-plate style. On 'page' the real 1619 scan slides in (public-domain scan; rights of the archive.org scan still to confirm).

short.hook_title: Kepler's sentence that ran the solar system

lines.text: In 1619, Kepler wrote a sentence he called most certain and most exact.
lines.visual: On 'sentence' an amber highlight sweeps the Latin 'Sed res est certissima exactissimaque ...'; a translation panel slides in.

lines.text: A planet's period grows with its distance to the power of one and a half.
lines.visual: Translation panel: 'the ratio of the periods is precisely the 3/2 power of the ratio of the mean distances'. Optional (first cut if tight): the equal-areas wedge sweeps, labeled '2nd law, 1609'.

lines.text: Plot the six planets he knew, and they fall on one straight line. His word for it: exactly.
lines.visual: Log-log axes, period vs distance; Mercury to Saturn drop dots; on 'exactly' they snap to a straight line, slope 1.5 (insight sting). Pull-back to the film strip.

short.hook_title: Kepler's sentence that ran the solar system

lines.text: Now show them how it's made.
lines.visual: Engraved-plate style. The prompt types; the orchestrator node appears on 'made'.

short.hook_title: How 9 AI agents edit a documentary

lines.text: One orchestrator writes the plan. Nine builder agents make the scenes at the same time.
lines.visual: On 'Nine' the orchestrator fans out to 9 agent nodes. Generic owner numbers tick in on screen only: ~1.1M tokens per finished minute, 54 % fewer than the previous pipeline, chapters render in 1-3 minutes, 9 builder agents in parallel.

lines.text: A deterministic GPU render stitches them together, cued to every word.
lines.visual: Scene tiles slot into a timeline; a word-level waveform runs under them and each tile snaps to its word on 'word'.

lines.text: Then the cutting room makes its cut.
lines.visual: Cutting room (~12 s across L4-L5): the strip stops on a light table; on 'cut' a splicer cuts this trailer's own P vs NP frame.

lines.text: Each chapter stands up as a Short, framed and captioned.
lines.visual: The frame stands vertical, a crop square locks on, captions write in on 'captioned'; it drops into a generic phone (no platform UI or logos) and a thumb swipes through 3 Shorts from this trailer. Pull-back to the film strip.

short.hook_title: How 9 AI agents edit a documentary

lines.text: End on the repo.
lines.visual: The strip winds onto a reel; the reel's spokes become Fourier epicycles that trace the logo.

lines.text: Every frame you just saw was made with this repo.
lines.visual: On 'repo' github.com/Fr4nzz/vibe-animator writes in under the logo.

lines.text: Describe the explainer you want. The agents build the rest: script, voices, scenes and Shorts.
lines.visual: End card: 'Every frame you just saw was made with this repo. Built with Claude Code + ElevenLabs.' Credits: manim-web, ElevenLabs, Claude Code, Kepler scan source.
